title: Which Vessels Relaxed?
endLine: The crossing slides along the unmoved line; its slope sets the direction.

scenes.tts: Cardiac output sits where the heart's rising line crosses the veins' falling line. Now a drug relaxes blood vessels, and resistance falls. Does right atrial pressure rise, or fall?
scenes.narration: Cardiac output sits where the heart's rising line crosses the veins' falling line. Now a drug relaxes blood vessels, and resistance falls. Does right atrial pressure rise, or fall?
scenes.caption: Cardiac output sits where the heart's rising line crosses the veins' falling line. Now a drug relaxes blood vessels, and resistance falls. Does right atrial pressure rise, or fall?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's plot and colour map without a reset. The flow-versus-pressure plot fills about 70% of the frame height, centred slightly left: x axis 'right atrial pressure (mmHg)', -4 to 10, ticks every 2; y axis 'flow (L/min)', 0 to 10, ticks every 2. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: BLUE = the heart's line; GREEN = the veins' line and filling pressure; YELLOW = the operating point (the crossing) and its dashed drop-lines to both axes; RED = the vein-collapse band from -4 to -2 only; GREY = axes and ghosts of where a line used to be. All lines are computed from the lesson's illustrative linear model (not fitted to data): heart Q = b + Pra with b = 3, drawn for Pra 0 to 7; veins Q = (Pms - Pra) / Rvr with Pms = 7, Rvr = 1, flat at Q = 9 left of Pra = -2. A small 'illustrative model' tag sits at bottom right all film. Ambient motion throughout: faint GREEN flow dots drift down the veins' line toward the crossing and faint BLUE dots drift up the heart's line away from it. Opening state: BLUE line Q = 3 + Pra and GREEN line Q = 7 - Pra cross at the YELLOW dot (2, 5), which pulses on 'crosses'. On 'resistance falls', a white tag 'resistance falls' drops in at top left with a down arrow. On the question, a white '?' appears over the x-axis tick under the dot, and the dot nudges a little right, then a little left, then back to (2, 5). Large white text across the top: 'Pra: up or down?'
Title card for at most 2 seconds over the still-moving plot (flow dots keep drifting): white text 'Which Vessels Relaxed?'. The question text from the hook fades out under it.

scenes.tts: Take one change at a time. If only one line moves, the new crossing must still sit on the line that stayed. So the crossing slides along the unmoved line.
scenes.narration: Take one change at a time. If only one line moves, the new crossing must still sit on the line that stayed. So the crossing slides along the unmoved line.
scenes.caption: Take one change at a time. If only one line moves, the new crossing must still sit on the line that stayed. So the crossing slides along the unmoved line.
scenes.visual: Same plot. Demonstration, schematic size: the BLUE line lifts by 1 (to Q = 4 + Pra) while a GREY dashed ghost stays at the old position. As it lifts, the YELLOW dot is pinned to the GREEN line and slides up and LEFT along it to the computed crossing (1.5, 5.5); no numbers shown. On 'the line that stayed', the GREEN line brightens and thickens. Then the BLUE line drops back to Q = 3 + Pra, the ghost fades, and the dot slides back to (2, 5).

scenes.tts: The heart's line slopes up. Slide along it, and output and atrial pressure rise or fall together. The veins' line slopes down. Slide along it, and one rises as the other falls.
scenes.narration: The heart's line slopes up. Slide along it, and output and atrial pressure rise or fall together. The veins' line slopes down. Slide along it, and one rises as the other falls.
scenes.caption: The heart's line slopes up. Slide along it, and output and atrial pressure rise or fall together. The veins' line slopes down. Slide along it, and one rises as the other falls.
scenes.visual: Same plot. On 'slopes up', a BLUE arrow traces up the heart's line. Two small arrows by the axes, one on the y axis and one on the x axis, both point the same way (up and right) while the YELLOW dot slides a short way up the BLUE line and back. On 'slopes down', a GREEN arrow traces down the veins' line; the axis arrows now point opposite ways (flow up, pressure left) while the dot slides a short way up the GREEN line and back. Labels: 'same way' in BLUE, 'opposite ways' in GREEN.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. Find the line that shifted, then slide along the one left standing. Move the veins' line, and output and atrial pressure go the same way. Move the heart's line, and they go opposite ways.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. Find the line that shifted, then slide along the one left standing. Move the veins' line, and output and atrial pressure go the same way. Move the heart's line, and they go opposite ways.
scenes.caption: So here is the rule. Find the line that shifted, then slide along the one left standing. Move the veins' line, and output and atrial pressure go the same way. Move the heart's line, and they go opposite ways.
scenes.visual: Same plot, both lines at baseline, dot at (2, 5). The rule builds as two short rows at the right edge, each appearing as it is said: a GREEN line icon then 'veins move: same way'; a BLUE line icon then 'heart moves: opposite ways'. On 'veins' line' the GREEN line pulses; on 'heart's line' the BLUE line pulses. The two rows stay on screen, dimmed, for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: Back to the drug. Resistance fell, but which resistance? Total peripheral resistance is measured from arterial pressure. With an illustrative arterial pressure, it comes out at eighteen. Resistance to venous return is one. So say which vessels dilated.
scenes.narration: Back to the drug. Resistance fell, but which resistance? Total peripheral resistance is measured from arterial pressure. With an illustrative arterial pressure, it comes out at 18. Resistance to venous return is 1. So say which vessels dilated.
scenes.caption: Back to the drug. Resistance fell, but which resistance? Total peripheral resistance is measured from arterial pressure. With an illustrative arterial pressure, it comes out at 18. Resistance to venous return is 1. So say which vessels dilated.
scenes.visual: Same plot. The 'resistance falls' tag returns at top left and splits into two white tags side by side: 'TPR = 18' and, in GREEN, 'Rvr = 1' (units mmHg min per L, small, under both). On 'which vessels dilated', those two tags fade out and two separate buttons appear, labelled 'veins' and 'arterioles'. Computed from the lesson: TPR = (92 - 2) / 5 = 18.

scenes.tts: Suppose the veins dilate. They hold more blood at the same pressure, so filling pressure falls. Only the veins' line moves, sliding left. Slide down the heart's line: output and atrial pressure both fall.
scenes.narration: Suppose the veins dilate. They hold more blood at the same pressure, so filling pressure falls. Only the veins' line moves, sliding left. Slide down the heart's line: output and atrial pressure both fall.
scenes.caption: Suppose the veins dilate. They hold more blood at the same pressure, so filling pressure falls. Only the veins' line moves, sliding left. Slide down the heart's line: output and atrial pressure both fall.
scenes.visual: Same plot. The 'veins' button lights. A GREY dashed ghost stays at the old GREEN line; the GREEN line slides LEFT, parallel, its zero-flow end moving left from Pra 7 (size of shift schematic, tag 'shift size schematic'; draw it to Pms = 5). The YELLOW dot slides DOWN and LEFT along the unmoved BLUE line. Arrows by the axes: flow down, pressure left, 'same way' row at right pulses. No numbers spoken or shown for this case. Then reset to baseline; ghost fades.

scenes.tts: A different case. Halve the resistance to venous return, and change nothing else. The veins' line tilts steeper, pivoting at its zero flow point. Which way do output and atrial pressure go?
scenes.narration: A different case. Halve the resistance to venous return, and change nothing else. The veins' line tilts steeper, pivoting at its zero-flow point. Which way do output and atrial pressure go?
scenes.caption: A different case. Halve the resistance to venous return, and change nothing else. The veins' line tilts steeper, pivoting at its zero-flow point. Which way do output and atrial pressure go?
scenes.visual: Same plot, baseline. A GREEN pivot ring appears at (7, 0). The GREEN line rotates about it to the computed steeper line Q = (7 - Pra) / 0.5 = 14 - 2 x Pra, drawn from (7, 0) up to where it leaves the top of the plot at (2, 10); a GREY dashed ghost keeps the old line. The YELLOW dot is NOT moved yet: it waits at (2, 5), now off the green line, flashing gently. Large white question across the top: 'Output and Pra: which way?'

Hold for about 4.5 seconds with the question still on screen and the plot as left by the previous scene: the tilted GREEN line, the GREY ghost, the waiting YELLOW dot flashing slowly. Flow dots keep drifting. No new elements.

scenes.tts: Only the veins' line moved, so slide along the heart's line. Both rise. Atrial pressure goes from two to about three point seven millimetres of mercury. Output goes from five to about six point seven litres a minute.
scenes.narration: Only the veins' line moved, so slide along the heart's line. Both rise. Atrial pressure goes from 2 to about 3.7 mmHg. Output goes from 5 to about 6.7 L per min.
scenes.caption: Only the veins' line moved, so slide along the heart's line. Both rise. Atrial pressure goes from 2 to about 3.7 mmHg. Output goes from 5 to about 6.7 L per min.
scenes.visual: The question fades. The YELLOW dot slides UP and RIGHT along the BLUE line to the computed crossing (3.67, 6.67); its dashed drop-lines follow, and axis readouts change '2' to '3.7' (x) and '5' to '6.7' (y) as each is said. The 'same way' row at right pulses. Check: 3 + 3.67 = 6.67 and 14 - 2 x 3.67 = 6.67.

scenes.tts: Arteriolar dilation does more. It lowers resistance to venous return, tilting the veins' line. It also lowers afterload, which can lift the heart's line. Two lines move, so take each shift in turn.
scenes.narration: Arteriolar dilation does more. It lowers resistance to venous return, tilting the veins' line. It also lowers afterload, which can lift the heart's line. Two lines move, so take each shift in turn.
scenes.caption: Arteriolar dilation does more. It lowers resistance to venous return, tilting the veins' line. It also lowers afterload, which can lift the heart's line. Two lines move, so take each shift in turn.
scenes.visual: Same plot, starting from the tilted GREEN line and the dot at (3.67, 6.67). The 'arterioles' button lights. On 'tilting the veins' line', the GREEN line pulses where it is (already tilted). On 'lift the heart's line', the BLUE line rises by 1 to Q = 4 + Pra, a GREY dashed ghost keeping Q = 3 + Pra. On 'take each shift in turn', the two moves are labelled with small tags: GREEN 'tilt', BLUE 'lift'.

scenes.tts: Both shifts raise output. For atrial pressure they pull opposite ways, and the larger shift wins. In this model the tilt wins. Output reaches about seven point three, and atrial pressure about three point three. Those sizes were chosen for clarity, not measured.
scenes.narration: Both shifts raise output. For atrial pressure they pull opposite ways, and the larger shift wins. In this model the tilt wins. Output reaches about 7.3, and atrial pressure about 3.3. Those sizes were chosen for clarity, not measured.
scenes.caption: Both shifts raise output. For atrial pressure they pull opposite ways, and the larger shift wins. In this model the tilt wins. Output reaches about 7.3, and atrial pressure about 3.3. Those sizes were chosen for clarity, not measured.
scenes.visual: The YELLOW dot moves to the new computed crossing of Q = 4 + Pra and Q = 14 - 2 x Pra: (3.33, 7.33). On 'pull opposite ways', two small arrows under the x axis: GREEN 'tilt' pointing right, BLUE 'lift' pointing left; the GREEN one is longer. Readouts: x '3.3', y '7.3'. On 'not measured', a GREY tag 'sizes chosen for clarity' appears under the plot. Baseline (2, 5) stays as a faint GREY ghost dot for comparison.

scenes.tts: So did atrial pressure rise or fall? It depends which vessels relaxed. Spot the shifted line, and the unmoved one shows where the circulation settles.
scenes.narration: So did atrial pressure rise or fall? It depends which vessels relaxed. Spot the shifted line, and the unmoved one shows where the circulation settles.
scenes.caption: So did atrial pressure rise or fall? It depends which vessels relaxed. Spot the shifted line, and the unmoved one shows where the circulation settles.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole plot: BLUE and GREEN lines at their final positions, YELLOW dot at (3.33, 7.33), the 'Pra: up or down?' text from the hook returns briefly at top and fades. On 'the line that moved', the line that moved last pulses; on 'the line left standing', the other line glows steadily while the dot sits on it.

End card over the dimmed but still moving plot (flow dots drifting along both lines, YELLOW dot resting at the crossing). Large white text, centred: 'The crossing slides along the unmoved line; its slope sets the direction.'
